chunk_findings.detail: `glob_clashes` still keeps only `pairs[0]` per conflicting other item in both the live branch (`out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0], lease))`) and the offered branch (`out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0]))`). Given a live lease held by `sw-cedefaults` on `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`, and a claim whose globs overlap all three, `conflicts()` returns three pairs but this function returns one `Clash` containing only the first pair. Since the `Clash` object carries no claim-glob list and no remaining pairs, `clash_report` cannot recover the dropped globs, so the refusal still names only one conflicting glob. Previous findings #1 and #5 still hold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:glob_clashes

chunk_findings.detail: The queue-behind messages now print `ahead.globs`, which is the whole set of globs the ahead lease asked for, not the subset of the refused item's own globs that are queued behind it. Given a refused item asking for only `brief.py`, while the ahead lease holds `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`, the new text says `those files (brief.py, lane_views.py, reporting.py) are queued behind ...`, even though only `brief.py` is the refused item's blocked glob. This overstates the conflict and does not pair the refused glob with its actual queue place. Previous finding #2 still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_guard_queued.py:25, ddflow/api/lifecycle/reservations.py:201

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` returns `[oid for oid, _lz, _p in clashes]` without deduplicating item ids. Once one other lease overlaps more than one of the refused item’s globs — the multi-glob case this change is meant to surface — `_ids` contains that lease’s item id once per pair, e.g. `["B", "B"]` for two globs on the same other item. The docstring promises “every conflicting item id (a waiter must wait on each)”, so a caller that uses `_ids` to append wait dependencies will wait on `B` twice. The id list should be deduplicated while keeping all text clauses.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` still has only the `held by {lz.holder} on {oid}` rendering and no queue-place branch. The bug this change fixes explicitly includes the `update --globs` path printing `those globs are queued behind sw-cedefaults` without naming a glob. For a queued clash passed through this function, the new text will assert `held by ...` even though the conflicting lease is only queued, and it still never states the queue place. The function needs a distinct “queued behind” branch for queued leases.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that both glob strings (`src/a.py`, `src/b.py`) and both holder strings (`HOLDER`, `agent-holder2`) appear anywhere in `main`; it never checks which holder is paired with which glob. An implementation emitting `"src/a.py ... held by agent-holder2 ..."` and `"src/b.py ... held by HOLDER ..."` would still pass, even though the entire promise is to list every conflicting glob with its correct holder. The test must assert the paired clauses, not independent substrings.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

chunk_findings.detail: The regression still does not exercise the `update --globs` queued path from the bug report. It only covers two live holders. A queued refusal that merely echoes the refused item’s own glob list and prints “queued behind sw-cedefaults” without naming the glob would still pass this test, so the stated bug can remain and the regression would stay green. The test should include an `update --globs` scenario with a queued lease and assert the conflicting glob plus queue place are named.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

chunk_findings.detail: `glob_clashes` still records only `pairs[0]` per other item (`out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0], lease))` and the offered-path twin). A `Clash` holds one pair, so later pairs cannot be recovered by `clash_report`. Given claim globs `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py` all overlapped by one live lease held by `sw-cedefaults`, `conflicts()` returns three pairs and the refusal built from this list still names a single glob.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:glob_clashes

chunk_findings.detail: Queued-behind text still interpolates `ahead.globs`, the ahead item's full request, not the refused item's overlapping globs. The same pattern is in `claim_guard_queued.py`. Input: the refused item asks only for `brief.py`; the ahead lease asked for `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`. The message says those three files are queued behind the ahead holder even though only `brief.py` is the refused item's glob.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/reservations.py:201

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` still returns every clash item id with no dedupe: `return text, [oid for oid, _lz, _p in clashes]`. One other lease that overlaps two claim globs yields two rows for the same id, so `_ids == ["B", "B"]`. The docstring says that list is what a waiter must wait on; a refusal for globs `src/a.py` and `src/b.py` both held by item B therefore records B twice.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` still always formats `held by {lz.holder}` and takes no queue place. A queued clash (the `update --globs` case the bug cites: files queued behind `sw-cedefaults`, not held) is rendered as `'src/a.py' overlaps 'src/**' held by sw-cedefaults on Y`, which asserts a hold that does not exist and never states queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only claims two live holders and checks that `src/a.py`, `src/b.py`, `HOLDER`, and `agent-holder2` appear as substrings before `Recorded:`. It never runs `update --globs` against a queued lease, and a refusal that echoes Y's own globs plus both agent names without pairing each glob to its holder (or queue place) still passes, so the stated bug can remain.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

chunk_findings.detail: The asserts never bind a holder to a glob. `src/a.py ... held by agent-holder2` and `src/b.py ... held by HOLDER` still satisfies `assert "src/a.py" in main and "src/b.py" in main` and `assert HOLDER in main and "agent-holder2" in main`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

chunk_findings.detail: The new text interpolates `queued`, which is built from the current item's own globs via `queued_globs(mine, ahead.globs, ...)`, into the clause “who asked for them first”. That clause still refers to the `ahead` item. When the globs overlap but are not identical, this now falsely says the ahead item asked for the current item's glob. Example: current item asks for `src/**`; the ahead queued item asked only for `src/a.py`. `queued_globs(["src/**"], ["src/a.py"], cfg)` returns `["src/**"]`, so the refusal prints “those files (src/**) are queued behind ... (ahead), who asked for them first”, but the ahead item did not ask for `src/**`; it asked for `src/a.py`. The previous wording correctly attributed `ahead.globs` to the ahead item but failed to name the blocked glob; this wording fixes the name at the cost of misattributing the request.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_guard_queued.py:26 and ddflow/api/lifecycle/reservations.py:202

chunk_findings.detail: The queued refusal still names only one queue-ahead lease. Given an update whose accepted globs are `brief.py` (queued behind `sw-cedefaults`) and `lane_views.py` (queued behind a different earlier item), `WG.queue_ahead` returns a single `ahead`, and `queued_globs(accepted, ahead.globs, cfg)` filters against that one lease only. The resulting message lists only `brief.py` and `sw-cedefaults`, omitting `lane_views.py` and its queued-behind holder, so the requirement to list every conflicting glob with its holder or queue place is still violated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:191

chunk_findings.detail: The new queued-path regression does not scope its assertions to the refusal clause. It checks `"a.py" in out.reason` and `QUEUER in out.reason` on the entire reason, but the other tests in this same diff show `out.reason` also contains a `Recorded:` section that can name the waiter’s own globs. A broken refusal still printing `"those globs are queued behind QUEUER"` without naming the conflicting glob would pass this test if `a.py` appears in the `Recorded:` section, so the exact bug this test is meant to lock down can remain and the regression stays green. The test should split on `"\n\nRecorded:"` and assert the paired queued-behind clause names the actual conflicting glob, not merely that the glob appears somewhere in the output.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_queued_behind_refusal_names_the_glob

chunk_findings.detail: `queued_globs` keeps every overlapping pair's `mine` glob and never dedupes. `conflicts` emits one `(mine, theirs)` pair per overlapping their-glob, so a single claim glob that overlaps several ahead globs is repeated. Given a refused item whose only glob is `src/**` and an ahead lease on `src/a.py` and `src/b.py`, the refusal is `those files (src/**, src/**) are queued behind ...`, which names one blocked glob as two files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:queued_globs

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression never calls `update --globs`, so it does not execute the refusal this change rewrote in `lifecycle.py` (`those globs (...) are queued behind ... The globs were not changed.`). It only claims a fresh item `Y` after a `queue=True` claim of `Z`. A regression that restores the old update text (`those globs are queued behind sw-cedefaults` with no glob), or that interpolates the ahead lease's full glob set instead of the overlap, stays green: `assert "a.py" in out.reason` is satisfied by any mention of `Y`'s own file, and `"queued behind"` plus `QUEUER` do not require the update path or a paired glob clause.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_queued_behind_refusal_names_the_glob
